source.title: The development of the nociceptive brain.

confidence_rationale: A focused review arguing the nociceptive system develops on its own terms and -- unlike other sensory systems -- cannot rely on prolonged activity-dependent shaping through repeated noxious input. This is close to a direct statement of INV-089's core: harm-evaluation quality is bounded by a maturation trajectory distinct from the exteroceptive (z_world) one. Confidence held below higher because it is a narrative review, not a single decisive measurement, and 'distinct timetable' is asserted across heterogeneous sub-findings.
failure_signatures: The review notes neurophysiological (EEG) and hemodynamic (fMRI/NIRS) measures of infant nociceptive development are 'not always consistent', so the exact ordering and rate of nociceptive-cortex maturation relative to exteroceptive cortex is not pinned to a single agreed curve.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The nociceptive brain matures through a distinct developmental process; unlike other sensory systems it cannot depend on prolonged activity-dependent shaping by repeated noxious stimulation, and mature nociceptive cortical network activity emerges on its own developmental schedule.
mapping.ree_translation: Directly supports INV-089's central premise that z_harm has a differentiation trajectory DISTINCT from z_world's, so productive harm-evaluator training cannot precede sufficient z_harm differentiation -- the biological nociceptive system likewise cannot be shaped like the exteroceptive senses.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The biological 'cannot rely on activity-dependent shaping' point cuts two ways: it supports a distinct trajectory but also warns that the REE analogy (train the harm-evaluator once z_harm differentiates) may over-assume that experience-driven refinement is the operative mechanism for harm at all. The mapping treats 'distinct maturation schedule' as the shared content and does not import the specific shaping mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Review of human infant + animal-model nociceptive-system development (spinal cord to cortex).

confidence_components.notes: High mapping fidelity -- the review's thesis is almost a restatement of INV-089's premise; source is an authoritative Fitzgerald-lab review rather than one experiment.
